subject: Culture
title: Feng Shui Architecture
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Feng Shui Architecture.

hook.text: Hong Kong's HSBC building has a gap in the middle so dragons can fly from the mountain to the harbor.

buildup.text: Feng shui arranges buildings to optimize 'qi'—the flow of invisible energy through the landscape.

discovery.text: Mountains behind, water in front, protection on the sides—the ideal feng shui layout mirrors military defense.

twist.text: Skeptics call it superstition, but feng shui spaces often score higher on environmental psychology measures.

climax.text: International developers in Asia hire feng shui consultants alongside architects. Ignoring it costs tenants.

punchline.text: Call it energy or psychology. The buildings still sell better.

quiz.question: What does feng shui aim to optimize?

details.summary: Feng shui — the ancient Chinese practice of harmonizing buildings with environmental energy (qi) — governs architecture, interior design, and city planning across East Asia.
details.whyItMatters: Feng shui demonstrates how spiritual beliefs directly shape architecture and economics. Hong Kong developers spend millions on feng shui consultations because buildings perceived as unlucky cannot be rented.
takeaways: Feng shui literally means 'wind-water' in Chinese
Hong Kong skyscrapers incorporate feng shui principles into design
Feng shui influences billions of dollars in Asian real estate decisions

faq.question: How does feng shui affect modern architecture?
faq.answer: In Hong Kong, many skyscrapers have holes or gaps to allow dragon energy to flow from mountains to the sea. Buildings face specific directions based on feng shui analysis. Interior layouts avoid features believed to drain positive energy.

faq.question: Is feng shui scientifically valid?
faq.answer: Feng shui has no scientific evidence supporting its energy (qi) claims. However, many feng shui principles align with environmental psychology — natural light, air circulation, uncluttered spaces, and nature views do measurably affect wellbeing.
